package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised via a sophisticated supply chain attack, where attackers injected a malicious backdoor (SUNBURST/Solorigate) into the legitimate software update process. This backdoor enabled covert remote access, command execution, and data exfiltration on systems running the affected versions, resulting in widespread compromise of government and private sector networks.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (trojanized DLL within Orion update package)
required_permissions: environment_vars (to perform environment checks and anti-analysis)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The injected code first checks for signs of a legitimate, non-analysis environment to avoid detection. If the environment is deemed safe, it delays execution using randomized sleep intervals to evade behavioral detection. After the delay, it establishes an outbound connection to a remote command-and-control (C2) server, registers the compromised host, and awaits further instructions, which may include downloading additional payloads, executing commands, or exfiltrating data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is not part of the legitimate Orion business logic and implements covert, unauthorized network communication with external attacker-controlled servers. The use of randomized delays, environment checks, and dynamic command execution is characteristic of advanced persistent threat (APT) malware, not enterprise network management software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain logic for stealthy outbound network connections to non-SolarWinds domains, randomized execution delays, anti-analysis checks, or mechanisms to receive and execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While some enterprise software may contact update servers or send telemetry, such communication is typically to known, documented domains, without obfuscation, randomized delays, or the ability to execute arbitrary remote instructions.
key_indicators: Outbound network connections to avsvmcloud.com and other attacker-controlled domains
Randomized sleep/delay logic prior to network activity
Presence of code obfuscation and anti-analysis/environmental checks
Dynamic loading and execution of additional payloads or commands from C2
Modification of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unauthorized code

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious SUNBURST backdoor code into the SolarWinds Orion build process, trojanizing the SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in official Orion software updates distributed to customers.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised Orion update, causing the trojanized DLL to be loaded into their environment during service or application startup.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on customer systems, remaining dormant until environmental checks are satisfied.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs environment checks to evade sandboxes and analysis, then delays execution using randomized intervals before initiating stealthy outbound network communication with attacker-controlled C2 servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes persistent, covert backdoor access for attackers, enabling remote control.

attack_chain.action: Attackers issue commands via the C2 channel, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or deployment of additional malicious payloads within the victim network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of affected networks and systems, with potential for widespread data theft and further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers to external, non-SolarWinds domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Randomized delays (hours to days) before network activity following service/application start
Presence of obfuscated or suspicious code within SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Processes loading SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll exhibiting C2-like communication patterns
Dynamic loading of additional code or payloads by Orion processes
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (with hash matching known trojanized SUNBURST versions)
Presence of unauthorized or modified DLLs in Orion application folders (compare against vendor-supplied hashes)
Unexpected changes to Orion DLLs without corresponding legitimate updates
network_indicators: Outbound connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure domains (as listed in public IOCs)
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to non-SolarWinds domains
Beaconing patterns with randomized intervals to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Orion servers for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com and other published SUNBURST IOCs. Regularly verify file hashes of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and other Orion DLLs against known-good versions from the vendor. Use EDR and network monitoring to detect randomized delays in process activity, code obfuscation, and C2-like behaviors. Investigate any dynamic code loading or execution of unauthorized payloads by Orion processes. Correlate file, network, and behavioral indicators to identify compromise.
